blog_summary: Adrian Colyer summarizes a KDD'15 paper that presents a machine learning framework to identify high school students in the US at risk of not graduating on time. The framework uses traditional academic data to train classifiers (Random Forests, Adaboost, Logistic Regression, etc.) to predict at-risk students early, before they fail grades or drop out. The Random Forest model performed best in ranking students by risk, enabling educators to prioritize interventions for the top-k% most at-risk students. The paper also explores feature importance to help educators understand which factors contribute most to the predictions. Colyer highlights the potential ethical implications of such predictive modeling, noting parallels to workplace performance prediction (though the authors do not explore this). The framework is designed to generalize to other adverse academic outcomes like undermatching or not applying to college.
paper_title: A Machine Learning Framework to Identify Students at Risk of Adverse Academic Outcomes
